newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY CLAIMS HAVELANGE WORLD CUP VOTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY CLAIMS HAVELANGE WORLD CUP VOTE.

text.p: FIFA head Joao Havelange said more than three years ago that he would back Germany's bid to stage the 2006 World Cup finals, German soccer officials claimed on Monday.
The German soccer federation (DFB), which is at the centre of a row with England over bidding for the event, said the FIFA president had given the country his backing at a ceremony in Zurich.

"We announced our bid in June 1993 with a visit to FIFA's headquarters in Zurich and I remember very well the first reaction of Havelange saying 'my vote will go to Germany'," DFB spokesman Wolfgang Niersbach said.
"The president of UEFA Lennart Johansson also assisted at the ceremony in Zurich."
Last Friday, UEFA announced it would be backing the Germans' campaign, angering English officials who also want to host the tournament following the success of last year's European championship.

But Niersbach said it was important that Europe avoided the kind of costly squabbling that marred the contest for the 2002 tournament between Asian rivals Japan and South Korea. The event was eventually awarded jointly to the two countries.
"A big mistake was made (in Asia) with two strong countries investing millions of dollars in big campaigns," Niersbach said.

"Everybody needs that money for the tournament itself. We should not make the same mistake in Europe. Brazil, Argentina and South Africa have an interest too and it is going to be hard to get it. There is only a real chance if Europe speaks with one voice."

Niersbach said UEFA's sudden announcement, which came as a surprise to the Germans as well as the English, might have been sparked by British prime minister John Major's plans to host a reception at Downing Street for delegates from FIFA.
He ruled out any idea of a joint Germany-England bid.
"There is no question of a co-hosting of 2006. That was an exception for 2002," he said. "The English F.A. knew in 1993 that we had put our hat into the ring."

The Germans have been talking about a bid for 2006 for several years. At the 1994 World Cup national coach Berti Vogts expressed his concerns that the country needed to work hard on its youth players if it wanted to be successful at the event on home soil.
The DFB claimed it was Germany's turn to hold a major international tournament again.
Niersbach said all of Europe's other major football countries had hosted finals recently, citing the 1990 World Cup in Italy, France's hosting of the next finals in 1998 and Euro 96 in England.
But England have not held the World Cup since 1966 while Germany last held the finals in 1974 and also staged the 1988 European championship.
The DFB stressed it did not want a battle with the English over UEFA's announcement.
"People are talking about the 'old Krauts' but we were not involved in any of this," Niersbach said.
